A_controlled_retention_residence.priority: PRIMARY — L4 (selective retention) is NOVEL (not found in 15 patents)
A_controlled_retention_residence.independent_claim: A method of controlling therapeutic residence in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) while maintaining CSF drainage through an endovascular CSF-to-venous shunt, comprising: (a) delivering a therapeutic agent into the CSF via the shunt; (b) selectively retaining said agent above a molecular weight threshold while permitting CSF passage; (c) maintaining CSF drainage through the shunt; wherein therapeutic residence in the CSF is increased relative to unretained delivery while drainage is preserved.
A_controlled_retention_residence.novelty_basis: L4 (selective retention) not found in any of 15 charted patents. L5 (controlled residence) not found. L7 (fail-safe drainage) not found.
A_controlled_retention_residence.design_around_risk: MEDIUM — retention mechanisms exist in other contexts but not in eShunt
A_controlled_retention_residence.eShunt_specific: PARTIALLY — retention works in any shunt, but the venous boundary (L6) makes it eShunt-specific

B_separation_plus_residence.priority: SECONDARY — L3 (separation) is NOT novel, but L3+L4 combination may be
B_separation_plus_residence.independent_claim: A method of delivering a therapeutic agent to the CNS via an endovascular CSF shunt, comprising: (a) delivering said agent at a location separated from the dominant CSF drainage path; (b) selectively retaining said agent while permitting CSF drainage; wherein the combination of separation and retention creates controlled therapeutic residence greater than either alone.
B_separation_plus_residence.novelty_basis: L3 alone is known (found in 2 CereVasc patents). L4 is novel. The COMBINATION of L3+L4 is not taught.
B_separation_plus_residence.design_around_risk: LOW if combination is non-obvious; HIGH if separation alone is used
B_separation_plus_residence.eShunt_specific: YES — the separation exploits the subarachnoid-to-venous spatial gradient

C_adaptive_exposure_control.priority: TERTIARY — most valuable but needs separate search
C_adaptive_exposure_control.independent_claim: A method of adaptively controlling therapeutic exposure in the CNS via an endovascular CSF shunt, comprising: (a) estimating CSF drug concentration from hydraulic state and dosing history; (b) adjusting drug delivery based on said estimate; (c) maintaining CSF drainage throughout; wherein therapeutic exposure is controlled without compromising hydrocephalus management.
C_adaptive_exposure_control.novelty_basis: UNKNOWN — needs PatSnap search on adaptive CNS dosing + shunt
C_adaptive_exposure_control.design_around_risk: LOW if adaptive control is novel; needs search
C_adaptive_exposure_control.eShunt_specific: YES — uses hydraulic state (P_CSF, P_venous) for exposure estimation
C_adaptive_exposure_control.note: C connects Position #1 (hydraulic state estimation) with Position #3 (drug delivery) — potential platform invention

flagship: A (controlled retention/residence) — L4 is the strongest novel limitation. B and C are secondary.
rationale: V8 found L3 (spatial separation) is NOT novel. The claim strategy shifts from 'spatial separation' to 'controlled retention/residence' as the primary novelty. Separation becomes a functional limitation, not the inventive concept.
